description.summary: bento's private connection to its shell

protocol.description:
The shell is the program bento's config names with `shell`. bento starts it and hands it a connection of its own through WAYLAND_SOCKET; this global is only on that connection.
Through it, the shell gets the commands and events meant for the shell, and asks bento for glass behind its surfaces.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Glass objects made from it stay valid.

request.name: get_glass
request.description:
Makes the glass object for a layer surface. The surface has no glass until the object gets shapes. Only layer surfaces show glass; it's ignored on other surfaces.
A surface can have one glass object at a time.

entry.name: glass_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a glass object

event.name: style
event.description: Sent once bound and whenever the config changes it. The shell's own surfaces line up with the windows by these: the gaps between windows and their corner radius, in logical pixels.

event.name: animations
event.description: Sent once bound and whenever the config changes it, so the shell moves as bento's windows do: whether animations are on, and how much slower than normal they run, 1 for normal speed.

event.name: toggle_launcher
event.description: Sent when the toggle-launcher action runs, like from a shortcut.

interface.name: bento_glass_v1
interface.description:
bento draws glass behind the surface in the shapes and paths it's given: it refracts and blurs what's behind them and lights their edges. Shapes and paths that come close melt into one piece of glass, so a surface can grow one out of another.
bento shades the glass itself, like everything it blurs, so the surface draws its content straight on it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The glass goes away on the surface's next commit.

request.name: set_shapes
request.description:
The shapes, as an array of int32 quintuples: x, y, width, height and corner radius, in the surface's logical coordinates. An empty array removes the glass.
Double-buffered: it applies on the surface's next commit.

request.name: set_rects

description.summary: set the glass's shapes, to fractions of a pixel

request.description:
The shapes, as set_shapes sets them, as an array of native-endian float32 sextuples: x, y, width, height, corner radius and melt, in the surface's logical coordinates. A shape's melt is how close another piece of glass has to come for it to melt into it, with the wider join a wider melt gives, from 0 for not at all; it melts into the shapes and paths before it in the array. set_shapes' shapes melt at 20.
Double-buffered: it applies on the surface's next commit, and replaces set_shapes'.

request.name: set_paths
request.description:
Glass in any shape: closed paths of quadratic Bézier curves, in the surface's logical coordinates, as an array of native-endian float32 septuples, one for each curve: its start's x and y, its control point's x and y, its end's x and y, and the number of the path it's in. A straight line is a curve with its control point on it. A path's curves come together, and the paths are numbered from 0 up in the order they come. A path's inside is where a line out of it crosses its curves an odd number of times.
Paths melt with each other and with the shapes as shapes do. An empty array removes them.
Double-buffered: it applies on the surface's next commit.

entry.name: invalid_shapes
entry.summary: the array isn't whole quintuples, has more than 16 shapes, or a shape has a negative size or radius

entry.name: invalid_paths
entry.summary: the array isn't whole septuples, has more than 64 curves or 8 paths, a number isn't finite, or the paths aren't numbered from 0 up in order

entry.name: invalid_rects
entry.summary: the array isn't whole sextuples, has more than 16 shapes, a number isn't finite, or a shape has a negative size, radius or melt
